note: 'Then the man of God sent word to the king of Israel: Be careful not to pass by this place' (2Kgs 6:9), 'So the king of Israel sent word to the place the man of God had pointed out. Time and again Elisha warned the king, so that he was on his guard in such places.' (2Kgs 6:10). The chapter says 'the man of God' and 'the king of Israel'; Elisha is named at 6:1 and the king of the Syrian war is Jehoram.
'and pleaded with Him urgently, My little daughter is near death. Please come and place Your hands on her,' (Mark 5:23); Luke 8:41 names him a ruler of the synagogue falling at Jesus' feet.

'But Jesus, turning and looking at His disciples, rebuked Peter and said, Get behind Me, Satan! For you do not have in mind the things of God, but the things of men.' (Mark 8:33). Peter had rebuked him first, at 8:32.

'Where the chief priests and Jewish leaders presented their case against Paul. They urged Festus to grant them a concession against Paul by summoning him to Jerusalem, because they were preparing an ambush to kill him along the way' (Acts 25:2-3).
'Joseph of Arimathea, who was a disciple of Jesus (but secretly for fear of the Jews), asked Pilate to let him remove the body of Jesus' (John 19:38).

'and after serious thought I rebuked the nobles and officials, saying, You are exacting usury from your own brothers!' (Neh 5:7). Nehemiah 5 is his own account and says 'I' throughout, so the citation carries Neh 1:1, where the book names him.
'As I urged you on my departure to Macedonia, you should stay on at Ephesus to instruct certain men not to teach false doctrines' (1Tim 1:3).
'and Peter took Him aside and began to rebuke Him.' (Mark 8:32), after Jesus spoke openly of being killed and rising again.
